input.question: Why is it that most insects instinctually flee or hide from humans, whereas flies will often just have a 'Whatever, I'm going to just fly in your damn face and see what the heck you're gonna do about it' attitude?
input.ground_truth: Because flies can fly. Imagine you're deep in the woods just going for a nice stroll. You see a grizzly bear... You're probably gonna shit your pants. Now imagine you're driving your car along the highway and see that same grizzly bear. You might slow down or even stop to get a good look. In both situations the grizzly poses a danger to you, but when you're in your car, you have a very powerful escape tool meaning if the grizzly bear did decide to attack you could easily get away. Insects that are slow are more likely to avoid potential predators, while insects that are fast are more likely to risk predators for potential food.
